items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
items.title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

items.summary: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.
items.title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media

items.summary: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.
items.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture

items.summary: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.
items.title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies

items.summary: Writing the Related Work section is a challenging task for inexperienced researchers, requiring significant time, effort, and skill. This study aims to ease this burden by introducing an ICT-based framework that automates the generation of cohesive and well-structured Related Work sections. We propose SciRelate, a novel framework that combines abstractive multidocument summarization and automated keyword-based subsection heading extraction. SciRelate comprises three main modules: (1) document clustering using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), (2) related Work generation via a fine-tuned Bidirectional and Autoregressive Transformer (BART) model, and (3) Topic keyword extraction using TopicFusion-MP, a hybrid method that integrates LDA, TextRank, and MPNET embeddings. Experiments were conducted using the NudtRwG dataset, and BART was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. LDA clustering effectively identified subsection headings aligned with ground truth structures. The BART model achieved high ROUGE scores: 81.53 (ROUGE-1), 76.19 (ROUGE-2), and 79.03 (ROUGE-L). TopicFusion-MP outperformed six baseline keyword extraction methods in four scenarios, reaching a top similarity score of 0.6398. This study presents a comprehensive, automated pipeline for generating Related Work sections, integrating clustering, summarization, and keyword extraction in a unified framework. SciRelate highlights the potential of ICT tools to support scientific writing, particularly for new researchers.
items.title: SciRelate: A Framework for Related Work Generation with TopicFusion-MP for Subsection Heading Extraction

items.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange must coordinate access to limited chargers with energy supply while considering both energy cost and carbon emissions. This paper proposes a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) for dynamic vehicle scheduling (VS) and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) controller for carbon-aware energy dispatch (ED). SFGH assigns EVs according to reductions in service delays, and TD3 controls battery operation to balance energy costs and carbon emissions while meeting the resulting charging demand. The model allows both PV and battery exports, accounting for export revenue and carbon credits. Simulations on year-long case studies show that SFGH--TD3 achieves the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) configurations.
items.title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations

items.summary: This archive accompanies Supplementary Table S15 of the ProReT manuscript. It contains historical K562 and KOLF2.1J research-script snapshots, execution manifests, environment records, SHA-256 checksums, and raw profiling measurements for the ProReT v0.1.6 multiple-myeloma examples. Historical files and local paths are preserved unchanged; current methodological and reference-resource descriptions are provided in the accompanying manuscript and versioned R package. Large GEO and LINCS matrices are not redistributed. Related software: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21943239.
items.title: ProReT Supplementary Data S1: Software provenance and archived research workflows

items.summary: A research field records its open problems in surveys, keynotes and community reports. Those are prose, written every few years, and nobody can ask them who works on a problem now or whether it was settled last year. We argue the problems should be data, and we build the system that makes them so: a hand-curated problem layer carried in unchanged, under an evidence layer rebuilt from a bibliographic index, joined by typed, provenance-carrying links in one graph database and queryable from one language. A language model does four jobs -- per-paper extraction, catalog grounding, per-paper status verdict, and idea generation -- each constrained to a candidate set so out-of-set answers are refused rather than stored. We report a study on two curated catalogs, database research (1,053 problems) and AI research (1,000 problems), each with a prior catalog-only graph. The rebuilt graph answers every question the catalog-only graph answered -- 47 of 47 on databases, 34 of 35 on AI -- plus questions the catalog-only graph refused: recent workers, untouched problems, methods tried, and outside papers bearing on a problem (336 problems, 770 works on databases). The capability we most wanted does not survive its own audit. Of 41 solves and refutes verdicts hand-checked against the papers, 9 are correct, 30 partly correct and 2 wrong; no refutes verdict (0 of 34) disproves an open problem, and only 1 of 7 solves closes the central question. We report that failure in full and draw the design conclusion: a status change must be proposed with its evidence and never applied, making the human reviewer part of the architecture. We close with the data-engineering problems this raises: entity resolution across curated and harvested layers, verifying model status claims, freshness under source quotas, and evaluation without ground truth.
items.title: Rebuilding a Field's Open-Problem Catalog from the Literature: A Two-Layer Knowledge Graph, and Why Status Must Stay Proposed

items.summary: This release provides R code, processed data, analysis outputs, and documentation supporting an exploratory investigation of a candidate circRNA–miRNA–mRNA network associated with triple-negative breast cancer recurrence. The package includes differential expression analyses, paired expression comparisons, probe aggregation sensitivity analyses, multiple-testing assessments, descriptive ROC analysis, and archived network and functional annotation results. Input provenance, software session information, and instructions for running the R script are provided. The analyses draw on publicly available GEO datasets GSE154255, GSE38167, GSE101123, GSE182471, and GSE43502. The proposed network represents a computational hypothesis requiring independent clinical and experimental validation. Patient-level survival analysis and direct circRNA–miRNA binding validation are outside the reproducible scope of this package.
tags: Triple-negative breast cancer، ceRNA، circRNA، microRNA، Recurrence، Bioinformatics، R
items.title: TNBC ceRNA Network: R Code, Data and Figures

items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum learning across multiple mathematical subjects and characterize scaling patterns with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate. Our findings highlight structured textbooks as both a scalable source of mathematical supervision and an empirical framework for studying the impact of data organization on mathematical reasoning. We will release the corpus to facilitate further research on structured mathematical supervision.
items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks

items.summary: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.
items.title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities

items.summary: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in persistent social environments, understanding their long-term social interaction capabilities becomes increasingly important. While existing research has advanced long-term memory and conversational context retrieval, less attention has been paid to whether agents can autonomously re-engage with previously inactive conversations. In particular, remembering a past interaction does not necessarily mean that an agent can identify when to revisit it, decide to return, or reconstruct the context needed for a coherent continuation. To investigate this gap, we introduce agent social re-entry as a multi- dimensional evaluation problem, distinguishing three complementary capabilities: Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing. We develop a shared-snapshot evaluation framework that measures these dimensions independently, allowing us to examine how conversational resurfacing and persistent memory relate to different aspects of social re-entry. Evaluations across six LLM configurations show that resurfacing substantially improves target conversation identification, while persistent memory is associated with higher rates of autonomous target-directed replying. However, neither improvement is accompanied by consistent gains in contextual reconstruction. These results highlight the distinction between accessing previous conversations, choosing to re-engage, and maintaining conversational continuity. Our framework provides a way to evaluate these capabilities separately rather than relying on memory retrieval or conversational response quality alone.
items.title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry

items.summary: Stationary learning admits an ideal-gas description under restrictive noise assumptions. In neural networks whose gradient noise departs from these assumptions, however, an entropy-scaling relation resembling a Maxwell relation remains approximately valid. We ask which thermodynamic-looking relations follow from scale symmetry rather than equilibrium, and how departures from the ideal-gas description can be quantified, for discrete stochastic gradient dynamics with memory. An exact rescaling of trajectories explains the entropy relation without assuming thermal equilibrium. Within a local harmonic approximation, self-adjusting weight norms yield a spectral equation of state whose virial coefficients are set by moments of the curvature spectrum, and coupled parameter groups can sustain stationary probability currents. Our central result beyond this approximation is an exact curvature-transport identity. Together with a finite-step loss balance, it decomposes corrections to the harmonic fluctuation relation into measurable curvature changes, finite-step remainders, gradient-memory correlations and finite-window drift terms. A related displacement-weighted curvature change provides a diagnostic of the arrow of time; its mean and second moment give a lower bound on the relative entropy between forward and reversed state pairs. We also calculate the activation-boundary contribution to curvature for rectified teacher-student networks with Gaussian inputs. Tests in sphere models, teacher-student networks and convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 support the transport description and identify limits of the harmonic and cubic-remainder approximations. These results separate symmetry-based relations from equilibrium assumptions and provide quantitative diagnostics of nonideal fluctuations in learning dynamics.
items.title: Finite-step statistical mechanics of scale-invariant learning: spectral equations of state and curvature transport

items.summary: At high redshift, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) both cools relativistic leptons and provides seed photons for inverse-Compton (IC) X-ray emission. These two effects link the particle content of a bubble directly to the soft X-ray depression used to identify a cavity. We derive a physical criterion connecting lepton cooling, bubble volume, enthalpy evolution, and 0.5--2 keV X-ray visibility, while separating intrinsic filling of the X-ray depression from detector-dependent cavity recovery. For uncooled electron populations described by a power law with spectral index $s=2.5$, minimum Lorentz factor $100\leqγ_{\min}\leq1000$, and maximum Lorentz factor $γ_{\max}=10^5$, the measured atmosphere of the testbed high-redshift cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537 requires 0.6--1.2\% of the pressure in radiating leptons to fill the soft-band deficit. Across the full tested ranges of $s$, $γ_{\min}$, and atmospheric properties, the required fraction is 0.2--3.7\%. Complete loss of this component reduces the enthalpy by less than 3\% relative to an otherwise identical adiabatic bubble at the same pressure. A low-cutoff control with $γ_{\min}=10$ and $s=3$ instead requires 18.9\%, identifying the poorly constrained low-energy spectrum as the main physical uncertainty. For a fixed atmosphere and spectrum, the required fraction scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$. The declining-pressure tracks show that the X-ray deficit can cross the adopted detection threshold while the enthalpy deficit remains below 0.4\%; the time of this transition depends on the assumed pressure history. Thus, high-redshift cavity visibility depends on both the surrounding atmosphere and the pressure-carrying particle spectrum. This criterion provides the physical basis for an instrument-specific recovery analysis.
items.title: The Conditional CMB Visibility of High-Redshift X-Ray Cavities in Galaxy clusters

The split‑Gibbs null result therefore has a further candidate explanation that DP1 cannot separate. DPS is unaffected. No file of earlier versions has changed. A pre-specified pilot testing whether a blindness-risk score computed before any target data are seen ranks the realised blindness (undetected and uncovered error) of diffusion-prior inference on real X-ray CT objects (2DeteCT) under simulated restricted access. Study DP-A: weak attenuation (F = 32,000), 240 errors × 20 bases. Study DP-B: bounded-reach control, 120 errors × 20 bases. Two samplers: split-Gibbs plug-and-play (primary) and diffusion posterior sampling (secondary). It follows the learned (VAE) pilot, arXiv:2610.28155 (reproducibility package doi:10.5281/zenodo.23392686). The analysis plan, decision rules and fixed result sentences were approved by the author, and predictions and calibration were committed by SHA-256 hash, before any trial. The plan was not lodged with an external registry, so the study is described as pre-specified; the files named PREREG_… are that plan (their names, and the word "pre-registered" inside the hashed plan and the dated log, are kept unchanged so that the recorded hashes still match). Version 1.1 (26 October 2026) adds a post-hoc check of the linear response used by the blindness-risk score, specified in a dated plan and approved before any computation (response_check_plan_v1.md, response_check.py, response_check_results.json, RESPONSE_CHECK.md). Under the plan’s pre-specified reading, the response was not adequate for either sampler in either study, so the null result for the learned score does not separate the learned prior from this approximation. The pre-specified results of version 1.0 are unchanged. README.md and freeze_log.txt are updated accordingly.

items.summary: Failures of deployed clinical artificial intelligence (AI) systems have often originated in how their training data were generated. Whether the programs that train the health AI workforce teach practitioners to examine data provenance is unknown. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the publicly advertised curricula of health AI education programs at U.S. universities, identified through a structured multisource web search between April and July 2026. Two investigators coded coverage of data provenance (structural, dataset limitations, or data management only), ethics, and sustainability; collaborative structure; technical prerequisites; and the disciplinary background and gender of named instructors. The primary outcome was provenance coverage at the structural or dataset-limitations level. Of 43 candidate entries, 36 programs at 25 institutional units in 21 universities were included. Ethics was covered by 29 programs (80.6%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 65.0 to 90.2), data provenance by 8 (22.2%; 95% CI, 11.7 to 38.1), and structural provenance by 6 (16.7%; 95% CI, 7.9 to 31.9). None of the seven master's degree programs met the primary outcome, and no program addressed sustainability. Eighteen programs included team-based work, but only 5 assembled teams across clinical and technical backgrounds. Of 92 named instructors, 76.1% came from computational disciplines and 3.3% from the social sciences or humanities; among the 51 whose gender could be determined, 66.7% were men. U.S. health AI education programs widely taught ethics but rarely taught how clinical data are produced. None addressed the environmental cost of computation, and most instructors came from computational disciplines.
items.title: Data Provenance and Ethics in the Curricula of U.S. Health AI Education Programs

items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
items.title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

items.summary: A research field records its open problems in surveys, keynotes and community reports. Those are prose, written every few years, and nobody can ask them who works on a problem now or whether it was settled last year. We argue the problems should be data, and we build the system that makes them so: a hand-curated problem layer carried in unchanged, under an evidence layer rebuilt from a bibliographic index, joined by typed, provenance-carrying links in one graph database and queryable from one language. A language model does four jobs -- per-paper extraction, catalog grounding, per-paper status verdict, and idea generation -- each constrained to a candidate set so out-of-set answers are refused rather than stored. We report a study on two curated catalogs, database research (1,053 problems) and AI research (1,000 problems), each with a prior catalog-only graph. The rebuilt graph answers every question the catalog-only graph answered -- 47 of 47 on databases, 34 of 35 on AI -- plus questions the catalog-only graph refused: recent workers, untouched problems, methods tried, and outside papers bearing on a problem (336 problems, 770 works on databases). The capability we most wanted does not survive its own audit. Of 41 solves and refutes verdicts hand-checked against the papers, 9 are correct, 30 partly correct and 2 wrong; no refutes verdict (0 of 34) disproves an open problem, and only 1 of 7 solves closes the central question. We report that failure in full and draw the design conclusion: a status change must be proposed with its evidence and never applied, making the human reviewer part of the architecture. We close with the data-engineering problems this raises: entity resolution across curated and harvested layers, verifying model status claims, freshness under source quotas, and evaluation without ground truth.
items.title: Rebuilding a Field's Open-Problem Catalog from the Literature: A Two-Layer Knowledge Graph, and Why Status Must Stay Proposed

items.summary: The way software gets built is changing dramatically. AI agents now create pull requests, select dependencies, refactor codebases, interpret test failures, and execute infrastructure changes across the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). AI agents are autonomous team members, but unlike human engineers, they are ephemeral - their reasoning, decisions, and tool calls vanish the moment the session ends. Modern Security incidents involving intent mismatch or injection are becoming increasingly common - forcing us to address AI Agents as an insider threat. No widely adopted standard yet enables agentic provenance and governance and its obvious that you can't hold an ephemeral process accountable. The git log was designed for human commits. It shows what changed. It does not show what an AI agent did, which model it used, which tools it called, or whether anyone was accountable for the outcome. Every governance framework, every audit trail, every compliance control in the SDLC was built around one assumption: a human made the decision. That assumption no longer holds. This shift introduces 3 main procedural problems (not addressing scale) - Supply-chain vector - The agentic coder is software, so it is a supply-chain security risk. Policy guardrails - How to ensure the agentic coder is compliant with the policies of the organization. Task-alignment - How to align the agentic coder on its tasks and goals. We introduce Agentic Process Evidence (APE), a signed, tamper-evident, machine-readable attestation of agentic processes, linking the sessions to their outcome (process-aware logging). APE enables Policy-as-Code control over the agentic processes, allowing for human in the loop only when it's needed. We support the in-toto style attestation framework, and the protocol is aligned with the relevant regulations
items.title: Agentic process evidence

items.summary: This research investigates recurring inconsistencies, context retention failures, and ineffective error correction in long-term interactions between humans and large language models (LLMs). Using a retrospective dataset of 1,271 ChatGPT conversations comprising 26,949 user–assistant messages , the study examines how AI systems maintain conversational context, respond to corrections, follow established instructions, and represent the status of completed tasks. A systematic screening process identified 495 potential feedback signals across 192 conversations. From these, 26 anonymized case studies were assembled to examine observable behavioral patterns, including contradictory responses, task deviation, unsupported claims of completed actions, loss of previously established constraints, and repeated errors following user correction. The study introduces context-state mismatch as an operational framework for examining discrepancies between the conversational record and an AI assistant's subsequent responses or claims. It distinguishes directly observable failures from user-reported concerns and cases requiring further verification. The findings highlight important challenges in conversational reliability, transparency, instruction adherence, and long-horizon human–AI collaboration. The paper proposes evaluation methods involving correction retention, independent verification, and tool-action accountability to improve the reliability of future AI systems. As a single-user observational study, the research does not claim to establish population-wide failure rates or definitive internal causes. Instead, it contributes original longitudinal evidence and a reproducible framework for investigating persistent limitations in LLM-assisted workflows.
items.title: Context-State Mismatch and Repair Failures in Long-Horizon Human–LLM Interaction

items.summary: Test-time compute mechanisms, such as retries, confidence-based escalation and non-local routing, are conventionally deployed as black-box additions to trained models. They typically add forward passes or halting heads, but give no structural account of what the extra compute buys or what it costs against the model's stability guarantees. We therefore propose a theoretical and empirical framework for test-time compute on a Latent Dynamics Model used as the memory. When an encoder's latent state $(q,p)$ is advanced by a damped symplectic (velocity-Verlet) step of a learned Hamiltonian, every mechanism that expands access has an exact phase-volume Jacobian, a bounded energy change and an exact latch-transport law. We split reachability failures into escape failures and reach failures. A Lorentz squeeze resolves escape failures by injecting bounded, re-absorbable energy. A gated canonical translation (a one-step channel across $C_T$) resolves reach failures at $\detJ=1$ exactly. We verify this certificate stack on a designed analytic testbed. Reaching just beyond $C_T$ with the squeeze requires energy that grows quadratically in the excess distance. The gated channel's energy cost equals the potential difference between its endpoints, which is zero on the matched channel measured here, and so does not grow with distance in this testbed. An untrained state-replacing map annihilates phase volume and erases stored charge, while the gated channel transports it. On a learned physics-structured memory, we show calibrated compute rationing and evaluate the scaling limits of non-local routing against a physics-free baseline. The main contribution is the formalization and verification of the certificate stack, not benchmark performance.
items.title: Certified Access: Test-Time Compute on Conservative Physics-Structured AI Memory

items.summary: Packing a 3D volume into a token sequence is not merely long-sequence modeling. Once the volume is packed, sequence order no longer encodes the geometry of the sample---so a positional mechanism indexed by sequence position can learn the memory layout rather than the object. This is a general failure mode for attention over packed geometric data. We introduce PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that separates memory layout from attention geometry. PACK3D keeps local neighborhood attention exact, compresses only distant context into contiguous 3D block summaries, and indexes every query-key interaction with axial RoPE on true token-grid coordinates rather than packed positions. Because the rotation is applied before a block is summarized, the query-to-summary logit remains a weighted sum of query-relative 3D displacements; compressed global context therefore stays spatially interpretable after packing, instead of collapsing to anonymous pooled content. We measure the failure mode directly. On a controlled synthetic task---train on one packing, change only the memory order of the tokens, hold the physical labeling rule fixed---learned positional embeddings and packed-sequence RoPE solve the training layout perfectly yet collapse under Morton, block-contiguous, and random repacking, while axial grid-coordinate RoPE stays exact throughout. The same coordinate system carries to real data: on Allen WTC-11 hiPSC microscopy, PACK3D improves over a parameter-matched 3D U-Net on the 15-structure joint task and over a matched learned-position local-global baseline, with controls isolating the coordinate system, not encoder capacity, as the source of the gain. A fused Triton implementation matches windowed-attention latency at 65k tokens while supplying the long-range context windowing cannot---so the operator is not only correct but trainable at scale.
items.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention

items.summary: Version 3 research revision. We study the part of a sensor field that remains covered after every failure in a prescribed downward-closed family. The model includes independent contact failures, weighted failure budgets and losses of entire fault domains. For a convex sensor cover with nerve N, we express the surviving region by a complex on the maximal faces of N: a collection of maximal faces is a simplex exactly when its common contact set cannot fail. This is a coverage formulation of classical nerve and Dowker duality, for which we give explicit comparison maps and prove naturality under increasing failure families. For n closed planar disks, all maximal nerve faces are witnessed by at most n^2 circle points. Exact rational sign tests consequently construct the full two-skeleton of the dual model without enumerating the original nerve or the coalition shadow. A separate Lipschitz margin theorem gives continuous coverage certificates for prescribed triangulated targets under the same failure rules. Recomputing five supplied fields completes the previously unfinished dense example: its two-fold covered region has Betti numbers (5,6), calculated from a dual complex with 130 vertices and independently checked boundary rank. The implementation, inputs, exact arithmetic conventions and verification records are supplied.
items.title: Sensor Coverage under Structured Failures: Dual Nerve Models and Exact Geometry

items.summary: Borrowed Youth: Demographic Change and Multinational Location Advantage explains how national cohort succession and international recruitment become firm-specific location advantages over a production commitment. Home-linked relationships, recruitment shared across foreign affiliates and admission institutions determine attainable replacement labour. Version 3.33.0 clarifies the empirical bridge and journal exposition. The model-to-data mapping distinguishes accessible worker stocks and annual arrival flows from their discounted service values. Table 3 now leads with the main engineering-life comparison, followed by the accounting and common-support benchmarks. The country equal-pricing contrasts are expressed as conditional investment changes holding total measured international services fixed, with full covariance and uncertainty preserved. These transformations introduce no additional test, observation or regression. The discussion relates demographic succession to resource bundling, human-capital access and multinational portfolios. The exact AI declaration, including all figures, is preserved. Previously reported scientific results are preserved. The article supplies an explicit economic bridge from project value to expected investment allocation under stated choice, capital-size, duration and disclosure conditions. It distinguishes capital expenditure from accumulated assets, whose interpretation additionally depends on investment histories, depreciation and valuation changes. The retained capital-expenditure analysis uses the existing demographic construction and controls. There are 82 matched records from ten firms and 36 after fixed-effect support. The nuisance design has rank 33; the five focal regressors have rank three. Independent projection confirms this failure. No duration coefficient, interval or p-value is identified; the result is not a zero effect. The public module reconstructs the aggregate rank and supplies licensed rerun code without redistributing issuer rows. The existing engineering-life asset comparison remains: 317 allocations from 32 manufacturers in nine hosts, contrast -110.25 (95 percent interval -520.28 to 299.78; positive-direction p=0.724). Joint positive pricing and rotation are unestablished (p=0.763), and the familywise contradiction test does not reject (p=0.712). Existing Holm-adjusted block probabilities are 0.113, 0.085 and 0.656. All original estimates, covariance matrices, equations, formal results and six figures are preserved. These conditional associations do not identify recruitment-caused host choices. The held Nitra-Puebla appraisal supplies a EUR106-226 million residual strategic hurdle and 2,834 planned direct jobs. At a five-percent reference rate this is EUR2,959-6,308 per planned job-year. The retained frontier states the additional net productive service needed to cover an assigned share, excluding previously priced labour effects and without fitting a recruitment share. Cost-saving bounds distinguish fixed-life value improvement from a unique switch across lives. No new sources or observations were acquired. The manuscript has 9,920 counted words, a 172-word abstract and 23 full substantive pages before references; the main PDF has 41 pages and the appendix 137. Regression tables retain three-decimal probabilities, no significance stars and economic magnitudes. Counts include abstract, text, references and transparency; separately placed exhibits and the online appendix are excluded. Start with README.txt. Current article, appendix and complete LaTeX are directly downloadable. Three current verified ZIP blocks and nine frozen complementary archives reconstruct the exact 1,908-file replication tree with 1,907 checksum entries. Licensed WRDS rows are excluded; subscriber queries and public aggregate reconstruction are supplied. Third-party rights remain. Literature PDFs are linked rather than redistributed. ChatGPT and Codex (OpenAI) were used in October 2026 for coding h

items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum learning across multiple mathematical subjects and characterize scaling patterns with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate. Our findings highlight structured textbooks as both a scalable source of mathematical supervision and an empirical framework for studying the impact of data organization on mathematical reasoning. We will release the corpus to facilitate further research on structured mathematical supervision.
items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks

items.summary: Raw surface EMG (13 shoulder and elbow muscles) and isometric force/torque recordings (6 channels), sampled at 1 kHz, from three chronic stroke survivors who performed a virtual reaching task in immersive virtual reality with their most affected arm. The virtual cursor was driven either by the measured isometric force (force control) or by the force estimated from EMG (myoelectric control). In myoelectric control, a patient-tailored assistive-adaptive algorithm projected the participant's muscle pattern towards a healthy reference pattern, with an assistance level progressively reduced across blocks. For each participant the dataset contains one session of 9 to 16 blocks (376 trials in total): a maximum voluntary contraction block, force-control baseline blocks and myoelectric-control blocks at different assistance levels. Each trial file contains the raw EMG, forces and torques, the force driving the cursor, the task state, the trial events and the trial metadata (target direction, block, assistance level). A configuration file per participant describes the channels, the sensor calibration and the block settings. The data are pseudonymised. The files are MATLAB v7 MAT-files that can be read in MATLAB and in Python (scipy.io.loadmat). See README.md for the full description of the files and variables. These data support: Nocilli M., d'Avella A., Berger D.J. (2025). items.summary: Raw surface EMG (13 shoulder and elbow muscles) and isometric force/torque recordings (6 channels), sampled at 1 kHz, from three chronic stroke survivors who performed a virtual reaching task in immersive virtual reality with their most affected arm. The virtual cursor was driven either by the measured isometric force (force control) or by the force estimated from EMG (myoelectric control). In myoelectric control, a patient-tailored assistive-adaptive algorithm projected the participant's muscle pattern towards a healthy reference pattern, with an assistance level progressively reduced across blocks. For each participant the dataset contains one session of 9 to 16 blocks (376 trials in total): a maximum voluntary contraction block, force-control baseline blocks and myoelectric-control blocks at different assistance levels. Each trial file contains the raw EMG, forces and torques, the force driving the cursor, the task state, the trial events and the trial metadata (target direction, block, assistance level). A configuration file per participant describes the channels, the sensor calibration and the block settings. The data are pseudonymised. The files are MATLAB v7 MAT-files that can be read in MATLAB and in Python (scipy.io.loadmat). See README.md for the full description of the files and variables. items.summary: Gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. We organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. Two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. A separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. For black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. The framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
items.title: Curvature Blindness: Material Inference in Stars and Black Hole Candidates

items.summary: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.
items.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture

items.summary: Writing the Related Work section is a challenging task for inexperienced researchers, requiring significant time, effort, and skill. This study aims to ease this burden by introducing an ICT-based framework that automates the generation of cohesive and well-structured Related Work sections. We propose SciRelate, a novel framework that combines abstractive multidocument summarization and automated keyword-based subsection heading extraction. SciRelate comprises three main modules: (1) document clustering using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), (2) related Work generation via a fine-tuned Bidirectional and Autoregressive Transformer (BART) model, and (3) Topic keyword extraction using TopicFusion-MP, a hybrid method that integrates LDA, TextRank, and MPNET embeddings. Experiments were conducted using the NudtRwG dataset, and BART was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. LDA clustering effectively identified subsection headings aligned with ground truth structures. The BART model achieved high ROUGE scores: 81.53 (ROUGE-1), 76.19 (ROUGE-2), and 79.03 (ROUGE-L). TopicFusion-MP outperformed six baseline keyword extraction methods in four scenarios, reaching a top similarity score of 0.6398. This study presents a comprehensive, automated pipeline for generating Related Work sections, integrating clustering, summarization, and keyword extraction in a unified framework. SciRelate highlights the potential of ICT tools to support scientific writing, particularly for new researchers.
items.title: SciRelate: A Framework for Related Work Generation with TopicFusion-MP for Subsection Heading Extraction

items.summary: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.
items.title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies

items.summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange must coordinate access to limited chargers with energy supply while considering both energy cost and carbon emissions. This paper proposes a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) for dynamic vehicle scheduling (VS) and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) controller for carbon-aware energy dispatch (ED). SFGH assigns EVs according to reductions in service delays, and TD3 controls battery operation to balance energy costs and carbon emissions while meeting the resulting charging demand. The model allows both PV and battery exports, accounting for export revenue and carbon credits. Simulations on year-long case studies show that SFGH--TD3 achieves the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) configurations.
items.title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations
